title: CABINET: Content Relevance-Based Noise Reduction for Table Question Answering

en.text: Answering a question over a table looks like it should play to a language model's strengths: the structure is explicit, and the answer usually sits in a handful of cells. The hard part is finding those cells. For any given question, most of a table is irrelevant, and that irrelevant content does not just sit there quietly, it behaves like noise. Large language models are known to be susceptible to exactly this kind of distraction, so their table reasoning degrades, and it degrades further as tables grow and carry even more irrelevant data.

One intuitive fix is to shrink the table before answering. Methods like DATER do this by decomposing a large table into a smaller sub-table and reasoning over that. The trouble is that hard decomposition is unforgiving: if the wrong sub-table is extracted, useful information is permanently gone, and no amount of downstream reasoning can recover it.

CABINET (Content Relevance-Based Noise Reduction), from researchers at Adobe's MDSR Lab, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Roorkee and published at ICLR 2024, takes a gentler route. Instead of removing anything, it learns a relevance weight for every part of the table, amplifying what matters and damping what does not. The answering model always sees the full table; it is simply steered toward the cells that count.

en.caption: Figure 1. CABINET versus DATER on the same question. DATER hard-decomposes the table into the wrong sub-table (losing useful information) and its reasoner answers incorrectly (38). CABINET removes nothing, weights the relevant table parts higher, and the QA LLM answers correctly (45).

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01155
Code: https://github.com/Sohanpatnaik106/CABINET_QA
The problem: irrelevant cells are noise

A table organizes information across rows and columns, but for any single question only a few cells actually contain the answer. Everything else is irrelevant to that question and acts as noise. Prior work has shown that LLMs are easily thrown off by such distracting content, and the effect worsens on large tables because they carry more of it. This vulnerability is precisely what CABINET is built to address.

The case against hard decomposition is a case for keeping information available. If a cell is merely under-weighted rather than deleted, the model can still recover it when needed. That is the bet CABINET makes: soft relevance weighting over irreversible removal.
The method: a relevance score for every token

The pipeline reads left to right in the figure below. The table is linearized into a string with header ([HEAD]) and row ([ROW]) markers, concatenated with the question, and passed through the QA LLM's embedding layer (steps 1 and 2). An Unsupervised Relevance Scorer (URS) then reads the embedded sequence and predicts a relevance score for each table token (step 3). In parallel, a Parsing Statement Generator describes, in natural language, which rows and columns are relevant to the answer, and a cell highlighter turns that description into a cell-based relevance score (steps 4 and 5). The two scores are linearly fused (step 6), used to weight the table content (step 7), and the QA LLM decodes the answer (step 8).

en.caption: Figure 2. CABINET's architecture. The top path is the Unsupervised Relevance Scorer (URS), which scores every table token; the bottom path is a weakly-supervised Parsing Statement Generator plus Cell Highlighter that produces a cell-based score. The two are fused, applied to weight the table, and passed to the QA LLM (OmniTab, 560M parameters).

en.text: The subtlety is that no labels tell the model which cells are relevant. CABINET treats relevance as a latent variable estimated through variational inference, and shapes the URS representation space with three losses: a clustering loss that groups tokens into relevant and non-relevant clusters, a separation loss that pushes the two cluster centroids apart, and a sparsification loss that drives irrelevant scores toward 0 and relevant scores toward 1. Each token's embedding is multiplied by its relevance score, so noisy cells are softly suppressed rather than deleted, and the whole system trains end-to-end through the answer-generation cross-entropy loss.

The second path supplies an explicit, question-level signal that the URS might miss. The Parsing Statement Generator is a fine-tuned Flan T5-xl, bootstrapped from only about 300 manual annotations. It writes a criterion for the relevant rows and columns, for example "consider rows with result as loss, and note the higher value in the score column," and the cell highlighter uses it to locate the corresponding cells and produce a cell-based score. Where the URS learns an implicit signal, this path adds an explicit one, and the two are complementary.
How the two signals cooperate: a worked example

The figure below uses a question about how many awards "two and a half men" received to show the division of labor. The URS assigns higher scores to the rows that are genuinely relevant (where the show won or was nominated), but it can still miss a row, here the 2006 golden icon award for best actor in a comedy series. The weakly-supervised parsing-statement module fills in exactly those cells the URS overlooked. The t-SNE plot on the lower right reinforces the point: the URS separates the table tokens' latent representations into two clean clusters (red for relevant, blue for non-relevant), evidence that the three clustering-related losses are doing their job.

en.caption: Figure 5. A qualitative view of the two relevance signals. The URS highlights the question-relevant rows (yellow); the parsing-statement module recovers a row the URS missed (2006 golden icon award, best actor, comedy series). The lower-right t-SNE shows the table tokens' latent representations splitting cleanly into relevant (red) and non-relevant (blue) clusters.

en.text: Results: new state of the art at 560M parameters

CABINET is evaluated on three challenging table-QA benchmarks: WikiTableQuestions (WikiTQ, which demands compositional reasoning and uses short answers scored by exact-match accuracy), WikiSQL (also scored by exact-match accuracy), and FeTaQA (long, free-form answers scored by Sacre-BLEU). The authors additionally release the roughly 300 manually written parsing statements used to bootstrap the weakly-supervised module.

CABINET sets new state of the art on all three. What stands out is that it does so with a single 560M-parameter model (the OmniTab backbone), while outperforming much larger GPT-3 and Codex based in-context learning methods. On WikiTQ it beats OmniTab, DATER, and a fine-tuned Flan T5-xl by 6.4, 3.2, and 4.7 absolute percentage points respectively.

en.caption: Table 1. CABINET's headline results across the three benchmarks (all new state of the art).

en.text: Not just more accurate, more robust

Soft weighting buys robustness as well as accuracy. The authors perturb the tables in four ways, row addition (RA), row permutation (RP), column permutation (CP), and cell replacement (CR), and measure the relative performance drop. The figure below compares CABINET with OmniTab on WikiTQ: under every perturbation, CABINET degrades markedly less. Under the harshest case, row addition, OmniTab drops 18.89% while CABINET drops only 11.46%. The authors also observe that CABINET keeps its advantage as tables grow larger.

en.caption: Figure 3. Relative performance drop (%) under table perturbations on WikiTQ. RA is row addition, RP row permutation, CP column permutation, CR cell replacement. CABINET (green) degrades less than OmniTAB (red) under every perturbation, indicating greater robustness to noise.

en.text: Ablation: both components pull their weight

Two ablations confirm the design. First, the URS's three losses only help in combination: applying clustering, centroid separation, and sparsification together lifts WikiTQ accuracy from 60.8% to 65.6%, whereas any subset gives little benefit. Second, the two relevance signals need to be fused: weighting the unsupervised score at 0.7 and the cell-based score at 0.3 is optimal (69.1%), while relying on the cell-based signal alone (λuns=0, λcell=1) collapses accuracy to 37.6%. In other words, the unsupervised scorer is the primary driver and the parsing-statement module is a complementary aid.

en.caption: Table 2. Fusing the two relevance signals on WikiTQ. λuns weights the unsupervised score, λcell the cell-based score.

en.text: Takeaway

The core lesson of CABINET is that you do not need to cut a table down to answer questions about it. By learning a relevance score for every cell and weighting softly, instead of hard-decomposing the table and risking the loss of useful information, the model keeps full access to the data while being steered toward what matters. Pairing a differentiable unsupervised relevance scorer with a weakly-supervised parsing-statement cell highlighter is both more accurate and more robust to noise than prior removal-based approaches, setting new state of the art on three table-QA benchmarks with a compact 560M-parameter model.

The approach has its boundaries: the URS learns relevance without supervision, the weakly-supervised module leans on the roughly 300 bootstrapping parsing statements, and the experiments center on English table-QA tasks. But the underlying idea, that soft weighting beats hard deletion, is worth carrying to any structured-reasoning task where a few relevant signals must be found amid noise.

zh.text: 让大语言模型读一张表格并回答问题，看起来是它的强项：表格结构清晰，答案往往就写在某几个单元格里。但真正的困难在于「找到那几个单元格」。对于任意一个问题，一张表里绝大多数内容都是无关的，它们对回答没有帮助，却会像噪声一样干扰模型的判断。而 LLM 恰恰对这种无关信息很敏感，表越大、无关内容越多，推理就越容易被带偏。
一个直觉的解法是「先把表格变小再回答」。以 DATER 为代表的方法就是这么做的：先用一个分解器把大表拆成一张小的子表，再让推理模型基于子表作答。问题是，这种「硬分解」不容错，一旦子表选错，有用的信息就被永久删掉了，后面的推理再聪明也无从补救。

来自 Adobe MDSR Lab、IIT Kharagpur 和 IIT Roorkee 的研究者在 ICLR 2024 上提出的 CABINET（Content Relevance-Based Noise Reduction），换了一个更温和的思路：不删除任何表格内容，而是给每一部分内容学习一个「相关性权重」，把相关的部分放大、无关的部分压低。答题模型始终能看到整张表，只是被引导着去关注真正重要的单元格。

zh.caption: 图1 CABINET 与 DATER 的对比。面对同一个问题，DATER 通过硬分解抽出了错误的子表（丢失了有用信息），导致推理模型答错（38）；CABINET 不显式删除内容，而是给相关的表格部分更高的权重，让 QA LLM 答对（45）。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01155
代码：https://github.com/Sohanpatnaik106/CABINET_QA
问题：表格里的无关内容就是噪声
表格把信息组织在行和列里，但对某一个具体问题而言，真正含有答案的往往只是少数几个单元格，其余内容对这个问题来说都是无关的。已有研究表明，大语言模型很容易被这类干扰信息影响，导致表格推理的准确率下降；而且这个问题会随表格增大而恶化，因为大表里携带的无关内容更多。CABINET 要解决的正是这种脆弱性。
相比「硬分解」这种删内容的做法，CABINET 主张用一种软性的相关性加权：所有信息都保留在模型可见范围内，只是被赋予不同的权重。这样即使某个单元格被低估，它也不会像被删除那样彻底消失，模型仍有机会用到它。
方法：给每个 token 打一个相关性分数

CABINET 的整体流程可以顺着下图从左到右读。表格先被线性化成一个带表头标记（[HEAD]）和行标记（[ROW]）的字符串，与问题拼在一起，经过 QA LLM 的 embedding 层变成一串向量（步骤 1、2）。接着，一个无监督相关性打分器（Unsupervised Relevance Scorer，URS）读取这串向量，为每个表格 token 预测一个相关性分数（步骤 3）。与此同时，一个弱监督的解析语句生成器（Parsing Statement Generator）用自然语言描述「哪些行、哪些列与答案相关」，再由单元格高亮器把它转成一个基于单元格的相关性分数（步骤 4、5）。两路分数线性融合（步骤 6），用来给表格内容加权（步骤 7），最后送入 QA LLM 生成答案（步骤 8）。

zh.caption: 图2 CABINET 的整体架构。上路是无监督相关性打分器（URS）给每个表格 token 打分；下路是弱监督的解析语句生成器 + 单元格高亮器给出基于单元格的分数。两路分数融合后对表格内容加权，再交给 QA LLM 作答。QA 主干为 OmniTab（5.6 亿参数）。

zh.text: 关键之处在于：没有任何标注告诉模型「哪些单元格是相关的」。CABINET 把相关性当作一个隐变量，用变分推断来估计，并给 URS 的表示空间加了三个损失来塑形：聚类损失（clustering）把 token 分成相关与不相关两簇，分离损失（separation）把两个簇的中心推开，稀疏化损失（sparsification）把无关 token 的分数压向 0、相关 token 的分数推向 1。每个 token 的 embedding 会乘上它的相关性分数，于是噪声单元格被「软性压低」而不是删除，整个系统通过答案生成的交叉熵损失端到端训练。

第二路组件负责补上 URS 可能漏掉的信号。解析语句生成器是一个微调过的 Flan T5-xl，仅用约 300 条人工标注「引导」出来（bootstrapping），它先写出一句判断相关行列的标准，例如「关注 result 为 loss 的行，并看 score 列里更大的值」；单元格高亮器再据此定位对应单元格，得到基于单元格的相关性分数。这一路提供的是「问题层面」的显式线索，与 URS 学到的隐式信号互补。
两路信号如何协同：一个可视化例子

下图用一个「两个半男人（two and a half men）拿了多少奖」的问题，展示了两路信号的分工。URS 会给那些确实与问题相关的行更高的分数（该剧获奖或被提名的行）；但它也会漏掉个别行，比如 2006 年金像奖最佳男主角（喜剧类）那一行。这时弱监督的解析语句模块补上了这些被 URS 忽略的单元格。右下角的 t-SNE 图进一步显示，URS 把表格 token 的隐表示分成了清晰的两簇（红色为相关、蓝色为无关），印证了三个聚类相关损失确实在起作用。

zh.caption: 图5 两路相关性信号的定性可视化。URS 高亮出与问题相关的行（黄色），解析语句模块补上 URS 漏掉的一行（2006 年金像奖最佳男主角，喜剧类）；右下 t-SNE 显示表格 token 的隐表示被清晰地分为相关（红）与不相关（蓝）两簇。

zh.text: 结果：5.6 亿参数刷新三个基准
CABINET 在三个具有挑战性的表格问答基准上评测：WikiTableQuestions（WikiTQ，需要组合推理，短答案，按精确匹配准确率评分）、WikiSQL（同样按准确率评分）、以及 FeTaQA（长的自由文本答案，按 Sacre-BLEU 评分）。作者还额外开源了约 300 条人工撰写的解析语句，用来引导弱监督模块。
在这三个基准上，CABINET 均刷新了 SoTA。尤其值得强调的是，这一切只用了一个 5.6 亿参数的模型（OmniTab 主干），却超过了基于 GPT-3、Codex 的大得多的上下文学习方法。在 WikiTQ 上，它相对 OmniTab、DATER、微调版 Flan T5-xl 分别领先 6.4、3.2、4.7 个绝对百分点。

zh.caption: 表1 CABINET 在三个基准上的主要结果（均为新 SoTA）。

zh.text: 不只是更准，还更抗噪

软加权带来的另一个好处是鲁棒性。作者对表格做了几种扰动：行添加（RA）、行置换（RP）、列置换（CP）、单元格替换（CR），再看模型性能相对下降多少。下图对比了 CABINET 与 OmniTab 在 WikiTQ 上的表现：在每一种扰动下，CABINET 的性能下降都明显更小。以最剧烈的行添加为例，OmniTab 掉了 18.89%，而 CABINET 只掉 11.46%。作者还观察到，随着表格变大，CABINET 相对基线的优势依然保持。

zh.caption: 图3 表格扰动下的相对性能下降（%），WikiTQ。RA 行添加、RP 行置换、CP 列置换、CR 单元格替换。绿色为 CABINET，红色为 OmniTAB；每种扰动下 CABINET 的性能下降都更小，说明它对噪声更鲁棒。

zh.text: 消融：两个组件缺一不可

消融实验确认了两点。第一，URS 的三个损失必须一起用才有效：同时施加聚类、簇心分离、稀疏化损失，能把 WikiTQ 准确率从 60.8% 提升到 65.6%，而任意子集带来的提升都很有限。第二，两路相关性信号需要融合：把无监督分数按权重 0.7、单元格分数按权重 0.3 组合是最优的（69.1%）；如果只用单元格信号（λuns=0、λcell=1），准确率会崩到 37.6%。这说明无监督打分器是主要驱动力，解析语句模块是互补的辅助。

zh.caption: 表2 融合两路相关性信号的消融（WikiTQ）。无监督分数权重 λuns 与单元格分数权重 λcell 的不同组合。

zh.text: 小结

CABINET 的核心启示是：要回答关于一张表的问题，你并不需要先把表裁小。通过给每个单元格学一个相关性分数并做软加权，而不是硬分解、冒着丢失有用信息的风险，模型既能保留对全部数据的访问，又能被引导到真正重要的地方。把一个可微的无监督相关性打分器，和一个弱监督的解析语句单元格高亮器结合起来，比以往「删内容」的方法更准、也更抗噪，用一个 5.6 亿参数的紧凑模型就在三个表格问答基准上刷新了 SoTA。
当然，这套方法也有它的边界：URS 的相关性是无监督学出来的，弱监督模块依赖那约 300 条解析语句的引导，实验也主要围绕英文表格问答任务展开。但「软加权优于硬删除」这个思路，对于任何需要在噪声中定位少量相关信息的结构化推理任务，都值得借鉴。

The pipeline reads left to right in the figure below. The table is linearized into a string with header ([HEAD]) and row ([ROW]) markers, concatenated with the question, and passed through the QA LLM's embedding layer (steps 1 and 2). An Unsupervised Relevance Scorer (URS) then reads the embedded sequence and predicts a relevance score for each table token (step 3). In parallel, a Parsing Statement Generator describes, in natural language, which rows and columns are relevant to the answer, and a cell highlighter turns that description into a cell-based relevance score (steps 4 and 5). en.caption: Figure 2. CABINET's architecture. The top path is the Unsupervised Relevance Scorer (URS), which scores every table token; the bottom path is a weakly-supervised Parsing Statement Generator plus Cell Highlighter that produces a cell-based score. en.text: Answering a question over a table looks like it should play to a language model's strengths: the structure is explicit, and the answer usually sits in a handful of cells. The hard part is finding those cells. For any given question, most of a table is irrelevant, and that irrelevant content does not just sit there quietly, it behaves like noise. Large language models are known to be susceptible to exactly this kind of distraction, so their table reasoning degrades, and it degrades further as tables grow and carry even more irrelevant data.

One intuitive fix is to shrink the table before answering. Methods like DATER do this by decomposing a large table into a smaller sub-table and reasoning over that. The trouble is that hard decomposition is unforgiving: if the wrong sub-table is extracted, useful information is permanently gone, and no amount of downstream reasoning can recover it.

CABINET (Content Relevance-Based Noise Reduction), from researchers at Adobe's MDSR Lab, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Roorkee and published at ICLR 2024, takes a gentler route. Instead of removing anything, it learns a relevance weight for every part of the table, amplifying what matters and damping what does not. The answering model always sees the full table; it is simply steered toward the cells that count.

en.caption: Figure 1. CABINET versus DATER on the same question. DATER hard-decomposes the table into the wrong sub-table (losing useful information) and its reasoner answers incorrectly (38). CABINET removes nothing, weights the relevant table parts higher, and the QA LLM answers correctly (45).

en.text: Results: new state of the art at 560M parameters

CABINET is evaluated on three challenging table-QA benchmarks: WikiTableQuestions (WikiTQ, which demands compositional reasoning and uses short answers scored by exact-match accuracy), WikiSQL (also scored by exact-match accuracy), and FeTaQA (long, free-form answers scored by Sacre-BLEU). On WikiTQ it beats OmniTab, DATER, and a fine-tuned Flan T5-xl by 6.4, 3.2, and 4.7 absolute percentage points respectively.

en.caption: Figure 1. CABINET versus DATER on the same question. DATER hard-decomposes the table into the wrong sub-table (losing useful information) and its reasoner answers incorrectly (38). CABINET removes nothing, weights the relevant table parts higher, and the QA LLM answers correctly (45).

en.text: Ablation: both components pull their weight

Two ablations confirm the design. First, the URS's three losses only help in combination: applying clustering, centroid separation, and sparsification together lifts WikiTQ accuracy from 60.8% to 65.6%, whereas any subset gives little benefit. Second, the two relevance signals need to be fused: weighting the unsupervised score at 0.7 and the cell-based score at 0.3 is optimal (69.1%), while relying on the cell-based signal alone (λuns=0, λcell=1) collapses accuracy to 37.6%. In other words, the unsupervised scorer is the primary driver and the parsing-statement module is a complementary aid.

zh.text: 消融：两个组件缺一不可

消融实验确认了两点。第一，URS 的三个损失必须一起用才有效：同时施加聚类、簇心分离、稀疏化损失，能把 WikiTQ 准确率从 60.8% 提升到 65.6%，而任意子集带来的提升都很有限。第二，两路相关性信号需要融合：把无监督分数按权重 0.7、单元格分数按权重 0.3 组合是最优的（69.1%）；如果只用单元格信号（λuns=0、λcell=1），准确率会崩到 37.6%。这说明无监督打分器是主要驱动力，解析语句模块是互补的辅助。

en.text: Results: new state of the art at 560M parameters

CABINET is evaluated on three challenging table-QA benchmarks: WikiTableQuestions (WikiTQ, which demands compositional reasoning and uses short answers scored by exact-match accuracy), WikiSQL (also scored by exact-match accuracy), and FeTaQA (long, free-form answers scored by Sacre-BLEU). The authors additionally release the roughly 300 manually written parsing statements used to bootstrap the weakly-supervised module.

CABINET sets new state of the art on all three. What stands out is that it does so with a single 560M-parameter model (the OmniTab backbone), while outperforming much larger GPT-3 and Codex based in-context learning methods. On WikiTQ it beats OmniTab, DATER, and a fine-tuned Flan T5-xl by 6.4, 3.2, and 4.7 absolute percentage points respectively.

zh.text: 结果：5.6 亿参数刷新三个基准
CABINET 在三个具有挑战性的表格问答基准上评测：WikiTableQuestions（WikiTQ，需要组合推理，短答案，按精确匹配准确率评分）、WikiSQL（同样按准确率评分）、以及 FeTaQA（长的自由文本答案，按 Sacre-BLEU 评分）。作者还额外开源了约 300 条人工撰写的解析语句，用来引导弱监督模块。
在这三个基准上，CABINET 均刷新了 SoTA。尤其值得强调的是，这一切只用了一个 5.6 亿参数的模型（OmniTab 主干），却超过了基于 GPT-3、Codex 的大得多的上下文学习方法。在 WikiTQ 上，它相对 OmniTab、DATER、微调版 Flan T5-xl 分别领先 6.4、3.2、4.7 个绝对百分点。

zh.subtitle: Adobe MDSR Lab 联合 IIT 提出 CABINET，用可微的相关性打分让一个 5.6 亿参数的小模型在三个表格问答基准上刷新 SoTA

en.caption: Figure 1. CABINET versus DATER on the same question. DATER hard-decomposes the table into the wrong sub-table (losing useful information) and its reasoner answers incorrectly (38). CABINET removes nothing, weights the relevant table parts higher, and the QA LLM answers correctly (45).

en.text: Takeaway

The core lesson of CABINET is that you do not need to cut a table down to answer questions about it. By learning a relevance score for every cell and weighting softly, instead of hard-decomposing the table and risking the loss of useful information, the model keeps full access to the data while being steered toward what matters. Pairing a differentiable unsupervised relevance scorer with a weakly-supervised parsing-statement cell highlighter is both more accurate and more robust to noise than prior removal-based approaches, setting new state of the art on three table-QA benchmarks with a compact 560M-parameter model.

The approach has its boundaries: the URS learns relevance without supervision, the weakly-supervised module leans on the roughly 300 bootstrapping parsing statements, and the experiments center on English table-QA tasks. But the underlying idea, that soft weighting beats hard deletion, is worth carrying to any structured-reasoning task where a few relevant signals must be found amid noise.

zh.caption: 图1 CABINET 与 DATER 的对比。面对同一个问题，DATER 通过硬分解抽出了错误的子表（丢失了有用信息），导致推理模型答错（38）；CABINET 不显式删除内容，而是给相关的表格部分更高的权重，让 QA LLM 答对（45）。

zh.text: 小结

CABINET 的核心启示是：要回答关于一张表的问题，你并不需要先把表裁小。通过给每个单元格学一个相关性分数并做软加权，而不是硬分解、冒着丢失有用信息的风险，模型既能保留对全部数据的访问，又能被引导到真正重要的地方。把一个可微的无监督相关性打分器，和一个弱监督的解析语句单元格高亮器结合起来，比以往「删内容」的方法更准、也更抗噪，用一个 5.6 亿参数的紧凑模型就在三个表格问答基准上刷新了 SoTA。
当然，这套方法也有它的边界：URS 的相关性是无监督学出来的，弱监督模块依赖那约 300 条解析语句的引导，实验也主要围绕英文表格问答任务展开。但「软加权优于硬删除」这个思路，对于任何需要在噪声中定位少量相关信息的结构化推理任务，都值得借鉴。
